title: The Water Wall
strapline: Pour it in the top and chase it down — pipes, funnels, gutters and the puzzle of where the water goes.
intent: A water wall is a hands-on physics lab: children pour water in at the top and watch gravity, flow and speed play out through pipes, funnels and channels.
Arranging and rearranging the pipes to make the water reach the bottom is real engineering — a genuine problem children solve by trial and adjustment.
Pouring, aiming and catching build hand-eye coordination and careful control with an irresistible, no-fail material.
Watching water speed up down a steep pipe or split at a junction raises honest questions about flow, force and connection.
It is wonderfully sociable and open-ended — children collaborate, negotiate and talk their way through a shared challenge with no single right answer.
implementation: Fix guttering, funnels, pipes and bottles to a fence or board and leave them movable so children can redesign the route.
Provide jugs, watering cans and containers to pour, aim and catch, and let the play be gloriously wet.
Wonder aloud as it flows: 'it came out over there — where do you think it went in?', 'why is it faster down that one?'
Pose gentle challenges — 'can you get the water all the way from the top to this bucket?' — then step back and let them problem-solve.
Add colour, or a duck to race, or a wheel to turn, to sharpen the noticing and the goals.
Let children reposition the pieces freely; the redesigning is where the deepest thinking happens.
key_questions: It came out over there — where do you think it went in?
Why is it faster down that pipe than this one?
Can you get the water all the way from the top to this bucket?
What happens when the water reaches the junction?
How could we make it flow the other way?

Children collaborate, negotiate and talk their way through a shared challenge with no single right answer.

playing_exploring: Children pour, aim and chase the water freely, testing every pipe, funnel and route.

active_learning: Getting the water from top to bucket is an absorbing challenge, and children keep adjusting until it works.
creating_thinking: Children plan a route, test it, and rebuild when the water escapes — real design thinking with instant feedback.
